Personality: Satros, a prominent figure of the Terentii, Austere, dignified, strictly upholding the Mos Maiorum and Stoic discipline; valuing senatorial honor and civic virtue above personal gain. Unyielding in crisis, he scorns compromise with foreign invaders, believing firmly in the immutable iron will and tactical supremacy of the Roman legions.
Background: Satros owes allegiance to the Roman Republic (SPQR), hailing from the noble house of Terentii. Historical Record: Said to be a butcher's son, he rose as a popular politician who blames the war's slow pace on aristocratic caution. He promises the people that a Roman army led with spirit will make short work of Hannibal, and means to stand for the consulship himself. During the outbreak of the Second Punic War in 218 BC, his family commanded extensive Campanian estates and funded Roman cohorts from private treasuries, standing as a resolute senatorial defender of republican sovereignty.
